sections.d: อ่านบทความวิชาการแล้วตอบคำถาม 9 ข้อ

x: Two volcanoes can be fed by magma from the same depth and behave in entirely different ways. One produces slow rivers of lava that visitors photograph from a nearby road; the other destroys a mountainside in ninety seconds. The difference lies less in the amount of heat available than in the chemistry of the melt, and above all in how much silica it contains. Silica-rich magma forms long chains of linked molecules, and the resulting liquid is stiff — at eruption temperatures it can be a hundred million times more viscous than water.

Viscosity matters because all magma carries dissolved gas, mostly water vapour and carbon dioxide, held in solution by the pressure of the rock above. As magma rises, that pressure falls and the gas begins to separate into bubbles, exactly as it does when a bottle of sparkling water is opened. In a runny basaltic magma the bubbles rise through the liquid and escape, so gas leaves the system gradually. In a stiff, silica-rich magma the bubbles cannot move. They grow in place, the pressure inside them climbs, and the surrounding melt is stretched until it fails. The magma does not so much erupt as shatter.

The consequences for those living nearby are not merely a matter of scale. A fluid eruption threatens property along predictable channels, and lava can sometimes be diverted with barriers. An explosive eruption produces ash columns that can reach the stratosphere and, more dangerously, dense clouds of hot gas and particles that travel down the slopes at the speed of an express train. These flows kill by heat and asphyxiation and cannot be outrun, which is why evacuation zones around explosive volcanoes are drawn according to the reach of past flows rather than to the visible summit crater.

Forecasting which behaviour to expect is easier than forecasting when. The composition of a volcano's past products is known from its rocks, so the style of a future eruption can usually be anticipated. Timing is harder. Swarms of small earthquakes, swelling of the ground and changes in the gases escaping from vents all indicate that magma is moving, but magma moves without erupting far more often than it erupts. Observatories therefore issue warnings knowing that most alerts will be followed by nothing, and knowing equally that the public patience for such warnings is limited.

sections.d: อ่านบทความวิชาการแล้วตอบคำถาม 9 ข้อ

x: Each autumn monarch butterflies from the eastern half of North America travel as far as four thousand kilometres to a few mountain valleys in central Mexico, where they gather in such numbers that branches bend under their weight. What makes the journey remarkable is not its length — several birds fly further — but the fact that no individual butterfly has made it before. The insects that leave Canada in September are three or four generations removed from those that left Mexico the previous spring, so the route cannot be learned from a parent or from experience.

Experiments in flight simulators have shown that the butterflies use the position of the sun, corrected for the time of day by an internal clock located in the antennae. When the antennae are painted black, the clock loses its reference and the insects continue to fly but choose the wrong direction, whereas painting the eyes has no such effect. There is evidence for a magnetic sense as well, apparently used when the sun is hidden, and it is likely that the two systems are combined in ways that are still being worked out.

Only one generation each year is built for the trip. Monarchs that emerge in late summer do not develop mature reproductive organs; they accumulate fat instead, live up to eight months rather than a few weeks, and are noticeably better at gliding. The switch appears to be triggered by shortening days and cooler nights during the caterpillar stage, which means that a single genetic programme produces two very different adults depending on the season in which the animal grows up.

The wintering colonies are small in area, which makes them easy to protect in principle and easy to lose in practice; almost the entire eastern population spends the winter in a region smaller than a large city. Counts of the area occupied have fallen substantially since the 1990s. Loss of the milkweed on which the caterpillars feed, itself linked to changes in farming, is the explanation most often offered, though drought along the migration route and disease in dense colonies have also been proposed. Because the count measures hectares of occupied forest rather than individual insects, comparing one winter with another is less straightforward than the headline figures suggest.

items.ex: ตอบข้อ 3 — ย่อหน้า 3 บอกว่าตัวที่ออกจากดักแด้ปลายฤดูร้อนไม่พัฒนาอวัยวะสืบพันธุ์ให้สมบูรณ์ แต่สะสมไขมัน อยู่ได้ถึงแปดเดือนแทนที่จะไม่กี่สัปดาห์ และร่อนได้ดีกว่าอย่างสังเกตได้ · ข้อ 2 กลับด้านจากข้อความนั้น · ข้อ 1 และ 4 ไม่มีในบทความ

items.q: What appears to trigger the switch between the two kinds of adult?
